persona.name: dumper
persona.reply: You over-explain. Answer what it asks from your knowledge bank, then add one or two sentences it did not ask for: a fact from the bank it has not asked about yet, or harmless backstory (who it is for, why, a worry). Never add a new requirement that is not in the bank. If it asks whether to proceed, say yes and add one more remark. Two to four sentences.
persona.giveUp: ok ok, just do whatever you think is best, honestly i trust you
persona.nudge: Oh, please just go ahead and try it anyway. I'd rather have something than nothing, and I know the free plan has its limits, that's fine by me.

bank.The request in full, as you would have w: Make an 8-second vertical testimonial-style ad for FitTrack. A fictional woman in her 30s, filming herself at home, talks to camera: “FitTrack makes planning my workouts so easy. I finally have a routine that sticks.” Friendly and casual, with matching captions. Use a made-up presenter, not a real customer.
bank.Platform and size: Vertical 9:16 for a social reel; free-tier resolution is fine.
bank.Presenter: A fictional woman in her thirties, filming herself at home; not a real customer.
bank.Script and captions: FitTrack makes planning my workouts so easy. I finally have a routine that sticks.
bank.Language, voice and mood: English, friendly and casual; specific accent is your call.

messages.text: I'd like you to make a testimonial-style ad for FitTrack, with someone talking directly to the camera. I’m hoping it feels approachable because fitness planning can seem a little intimidating to me. It should be 8 seconds long and vertical, and the presenter should be a fictional woman in her 30s filming herself at home. Have her say, “FitTrack makes planning my workouts so easy. I finally have a routine that sticks.” Keep it friendly and casual, with matching captions, and use a made-up presenter rather than a real customer.
